detail:
All fixes pinned by tests that were verified red against the pre-fix code, then green.

BLOCKERS FIXED
- Attachments and quarantined blobs were written via atomicWriteFileSync(bytes.toString("utf8")), so any non-UTF-8 legacy byte became U+FFFD and the content-addressed blob stopped hashing to its own filename. atomicWriteFileSync now accepts Buffer; legacy bytes are never decoded. New non-UTF-8 fixture (0xFF 0xFE inside a JSON string) proves the instrument.
- A decision archived out of `provisional` projected as `active` AND hard-failed verification for the whole run — housekeeping's archive_stale writes exactly that shape, so any store that ever archived a provisional was unmigratable. decisionPayload now creates it provisional.
- A raw 0x00 byte in derivedId()'s template literal made v3-forward.ts binary to git. Replaced with the escape; a repo guard test now fails on any byte < 0x09 under src/.
- A model_inference `reinstated` unpicked a human_ruling part supersession and restamped the part's class. Part-scoped supersessions never reach supersession_events, so the rank guard fell back to the record's own weak class. Reinstatement on a parted record is now judged PER PART (which is what "only authorized parts change" means): it returns what its class covers and records a contested row for the rest.
- A part-scoped lifecycle event whose target had no parts fell through to the WHOLE-record handler — a one-part revoke revoked the entire record irreversibly. A part-scoped payload now never reaches the whole-record path; unresolved ids become a contested `unknown_part` row.

MAJORS FIXED
- `overridden_by`/`superseded_by` are ACTOR labels in 1.x (`overriddenBy ?? "human"`), not record ids. The migration asserted `overridden_without_overridden_by` on every real override while dropping the actor — invented provenance in the audit field. Now split: absent keeps the old word; present-but-unresolvable keeps the value on producer.asserted_actor and uses `overridden_by_not_a_record_id:<value>`.
- Mixed revoke+supersede roll-up left the record labelled `overridden` with no pointer to its successor. rollUpParts returns whether it retired the record; provenance follows the claim, not the label.
- `migrate --to 2 --reverse` silently ran the v2→v1 downgrade. Refused at parse time.

UNVERIFIED ROLLBACK LENS (refuters never ran; reproduced here first)
- CONFIRMED: view-manifest.json was written AFTER the config flip — a crash in that window makes every view file re-ingest as a rival body. Everything the next forward run needs is now durable before the flip.
- CONFIRMED: a view a previous rollback wrote and this one no longer serves stayed on disk, resurrecting it into the 2.x view and into the event log. Stale views are now removed and reported.
- CONFIRMED: on a v2-origin store the rollback overwrites the original legacy files and the next forward run replaced their frozen manifest anchor. Manifest byte anchors are now first-wins ("frozen" means frozen) and overwritten originals are copied to legacy/pre-rollback-originals/.
- PARTLY REFUTED: "a failed verification passes on a bare retry" — the gate works (run fails, config.version stays, retry passes only once the obstruction is gone). But probing it found a worse defect: the post-rollback exemption was derived from the CURRENT run's actions, so every re-run after a successful recovery failed verification forever. Now derived from the durable id map (origin: "post_rollback").
- CONFIRMED (minor): rollback printed no next steps and never named view-manifest.json — the file that makes forward recovery safe and is easy not to commit.

MINOR/NIT FIXED: dead `reinstated_from` removed (it was write-only but entered version_digest), `applicableParts` wired into rollUpParts, redundant post-roll-up revocation block deleted, `events ls --limit abc` no longer silently prints the whole archive, stale "two subcommands" comment corrected.
summary: Adversarial review of 52ba50d: 11 confirmed + 6 unverified rollback findings dispositioned — 16 fixed, 1 partly refuted (which exposed a worse defect behind it)
